messages:
devon: prod alert — scale controller in eu-west1 is oscillating during the last 6m. GPU pools not coming up, routing fallback to us-central spiked. Anyone already looking?
li: seeing the same. our nodepool API calls to GCE are returning 500s intermittently. rate limit? or quota? :confused:
oncall-bot: [ALERT] inference-scale-controller:eu-west1 HIGH_ERROR_RATE (avg 28m) — auto-retry inhibited. Incident created: INC-2026-178812.
maya: copying logs now. scale-controller logs show many duplicate resource metrics in a short window, then failing to bind ephemeral ENIs. snippet:```
I0321 14:01:12.345 scale.go:213] Received metric: queue_len=124 inflight=3
I0321 14:01:12.347 ec2client.go:87] AllocateENI failed: ErrThrottled: rate exceeded
I0321 14:01:12.350 decision.go:98] Decision: scale_up=40 nodes -> api call returned 500
```
sam: based on that, looks like NAT gateway TCP churn in the region—we saw similar in staging a month ago. Throttles cause controller to re-evaluate and then flip back when partial responses arrive -> thrash.
felix: @devon can you post output of `kubectl get nodes -o wide --selector=pool=gpu-eu` ?
devon: pasted:```
NAME                          STATUS     ROLES    AGE   VERSION
gpu-eu-1                      NotReady   <none>   2m    v1.25
gpu-eu-2                      NotReady   <none>   2m    v1.25
gpu-eu-3                      NotReady   <none>   1m    v1.25
```
li: control-plane reports intermittent TLS timeouts to cloud API, and cloud console shows multiple failed ENI alloc attempts.
maya: traffic to inference-hosts in eu-west1 is being punted to us-central via our smart-router, latency up ~180ms for affected customers. Dashboard: https://metrics/redwood/inference/regions
ops: material impact? any SLO breaches yet?
devon: some customers hitting higher tail latency, not SLO breaches yet but error budget burn accelerating.
infra-bot: [AUTOMATION] routing-policy: fallback-region=us-central activated for all eu-west1 traffic above 70% failed_capacity.
sam: short term mitigation: bump scale-controller cooldown from 30s -> 120s to avoid rapid oscillation, and disable proactive scale-to-capacity until ENI errors subside. I'll push a config change to canary.
devon: please also add an explicit limit to max_concurrent_scale_ops=4 (we were doing 12).
maya: started traffic reshuffle job to rebalance across dedicated pools: `trafficctl shift --from eu-west1 --to eu-central --pct 35 --dry-run=false` (running now).
li: verifying cost implications: shifting to eu-central will use reserved GPUs in dedicated pool but increases inter-region egress a bit. estimate +$2.3k/hr if sustained.
felix: can we instead preferentially route to local dedicated spare pool in eu-west1 (pool-id: dp-eu-standby)? I think we have 12 reserved there.
sam: dp-eu-standby is at 90% commit due to scheduled jobs. We can preempt lower-priority batch but need approval. cc @ops
ops: approve preempt of non-critical batch jobs for next 2h to free up 8 GPUs.
devon: preemption executed, 7 GPUs freed and attached to inference pool. nodes coming Ready now.
maya: scale-controller reports steady metrics now, queue_len dropping, inflight stable. :thumbsup:
oncall-bot: [UPDATE] Incident INC-2026-178812: automated fallback and cooldown changes applied. Monitoring for 30m.
li: root cause hypothesis: cloud NAT/ENI throttling + high burst of inference requests from a new ad-hoc campaign created sudden scale demand, controller reacted aggressively and then thrashed due to API errors. We'll need guardrails.
sam: immediate postmortem actions: (1) add backoff + idempotent ENI allocation, (2) honor cloud API 429 with exponential backoff in controller, (3) increase default cooldown to 90s for GPU pools, (4) add capacity-aware routing to avoid cross-region fallback unless no local dedicated capacity.
felix: logging action: add metric `scale_api_error_rate` and alarm at 5% over 5m.
devon: I'll own the follow-up. Creating follow-up ticket: INFRA-5234.
ops: good work. keep an eye for any replays from the ad-campaign — notify growth to throttle if needed.
maya: post-incident: customers impacted list exported and emails queued for CS.
li: updating incident doc and will attach logs.
oncall-bot: [RESOLVE] Incident INC-2026-178812: services recovered, monitoring green for 45m.
devon: final notes — temporary config revert scheduled in 4h if no regressions.
